precepts.text: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. So we fell by the edge of the sword, and we were led away as slaves into all nations. That is what happened to us. That is the falling away, and that is the precept for it.
precepts.point: And that man of sin be revealed. So instead of saying antichrist, Paul said the man of sin. The man of sin has to be revealed. The son of perdition. He also called the man of sin the son of perdition. He is talking about the same people John was talking about.

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.why:
“for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” What is the falling away? Slavery, captivity. And the precept for it is Luke: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

We fell by the edge of the sword, and we were led away as slaves into all nations. That is what happened to us. Before Christ returns, Israel had to fall away, and that falling away goes into a lot: it goes into us even forgetting our nationality and all of that.

The apostles asked Christ what they had to look for before his return and for the end, and Paul is explaining the same thing here. “Let no man deceive you by any means” is the same thing Christ said: don’t let anybody deceive you. All the prophets say the same thing in different words. Christ said Israel would be led captive until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled; Paul says the day of the Lord shall not come except there come a falling away first.

And while Israel is in that captivity, “that man of sin” must “be revealed, the son of perdition.” Instead of saying antichrist, Paul says the man of sin. It is not one person but a race, a people: Edom, the one Malachi says the prophets “shall call them, The border of wickedness.” That is the time we are living in now, with Israel fallen away into all nations and the prophets revealing the wicked, and that is why the day of the Lord has not yet come.

precepts.text: They shall fall by the edge of the sword: the Israelites. And shall be led away captive into all nations: slavery. And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles: Jerusalem shall be taken over by other nations, in particular Edomite nations, until that time of rulership is fulfilled.
precepts.point: Definition read in class: perdition primarily refers to eternal damnation or the state of spiritual ruin and hell, originating from the Latin word perdere, meaning to destroy or to lose. The noun is often used to describe the fate of the wicked or the absolute loss of one's soul. In Christian theology it signifies the final loss of salvation and the unending punishment of a soul in the afterlife.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
Paul says “that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” The falling away is not people leaving Christianity to join Islam, the way Christians read it. The falling away means the twelve tribes of Israel have to fall and go into captivity, and Luke 21:24 shows it.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites. “and shall be led away captive into all nations”: slavery. “and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Jerusalem taken over by other nations, in particular the Edomite nations, “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”, until that time of rulership is over.

So two things have to happen before Christ returns: all twelve tribes must go into captivity, which is where we are now, and the man of sin must be revealed, the son of perdition. Perdition means eternal damnation, spiritual ruin and hell; it comes from the Latin perdere, to destroy or to lose. It is the fate of the wicked, the absolute loss of one's soul, the final loss of salvation and unending punishment.

precepts.text: When ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, the Roman armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. It was prophesied that Jerusalem would be destroyed. Let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains: our people fled into Africa. Rudolph R. Windsor's book Babylon to Timbuktu records that the Israelites fled from Roman persecution and slavery, that the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves, and it records the outrageous atrocities the Romans committed against our people in that destruction. These be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled: the judgment of Deuteronomy for breaking the laws all the way back to Moses. They shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: our people were led into slavery into all nations, and everywhere we have gone we have been their sweat equity. The world economy was built off of our destruction. And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled: the people on the land now calling themselves Jews are the Gentiles the Lord spoke of, and when their time is up, Psalms 149 is what awaits them.
precepts.point: The woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God. The wilderness is Africa; we fled out of Jerusalem into Africa, the same place where Joseph took the young child and his mother. Then a place was prepared, which is the Americas. A thousand two hundred and threescore days: 1260 days, three and a half, the same period written as forty and two months and as a time, times, and the dividing of time in Daniel 7 and 8.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
The dragon's tail “drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth”: cast the Israelites into captivity and slavery. The third part is mainly Judah, Benjamin and Levi, with stragglers of the other tribes, like Anna of the tribe of Aser, still in Jerusalem; the bulk of the tribes had already gone under Cyrus. This is going into 70 AD, and Luke tells it.

“And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” The Roman armies. It was prophesied that Jerusalem would be destroyed. “Then let them which are in Judea flee to the mountains”: our people fled into Egypt, into Africa, the same place Joseph took Jesus and his mother. Rudolph R. Windsor's book Babylon to Timbuktu records that the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves. “and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto”: the other tribes were already gone, the twelve tribes scattered abroad.

“For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled”: it was time for the judgment for breaking the laws all the way back to Moses. “there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people”: the Romans chopped up our babies and the pregnant women. They did not care. And he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword; they will pay for this.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations.” Everywhere we have gone, we have been the nations' sweat equity. The world economy was built off the destruction of our babies, our mothers and fathers, and the whole earth rejoices over it.

“and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” The land has white people on it calling themselves us; the Lord calls them the Gentiles. When their time is up, Psalms 149 is where they are going.

precepts.text: And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. The Roman armies: the desolation Daniel determined.
precepts.point: So Christ's seventy times seven is the 490: the prophecy completed, the perfection of mercy delivered exactly on schedule, because we could not sacrifice in our captivities and needed him.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: cut off for the children of Israel. “and the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”. That prince that shall come and destroy the sanctuary is Titus. “and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.” The flood is 70 AD, the destruction, and us being led away into captivity.

Christ spoke of that same desolation: “And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” What armies? The Roman armies. That is what Daniel 9:26 is speaking of, the prince that shall come and destroy the city and the sanctuary.

Then Daniel 9:27: “in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”: the temple being destroyed. “and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation”. The Roman armies around Jerusalem were the sign that the desolation determined in the seventy weeks was at hand.

So the 490 years end with Christ cut off for us and the desolation of the city by Titus. After that there was no sacrifice for us but Christ, and that is why his sacrifice is our only way through to perfection.

precepts.text: Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Christ told the Samaritan woman the Israelites would not be worshipping in Jerusalem and not in Samaria: he's saying what we read in Luke 21, that we would be carried away as slaves into all nations.
precepts.point: An old map drawn by Esau was shown in class, found by Captain Joel in a library archive: Jewish communities marked all over Africa, the Elephantine Jews, Levite cities in Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms of Ganata and Kamnuri, the Berber Jews of the north. Esau knew where we were in Africa; they drew this map to pinpoint us. Why did they need to know where we were? Because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Christ told the Samaritan woman by the well the same thing he said in Luke 21. She said, “Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet. Our fathers worshipped in this mountain; and ye say, that in Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.” The Samaritans worshipped up on Mount Gerizim, because their fathers used to worship up there back in the days.

“Jesus saith unto her, Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what”. The Samaritans were not going to worship in that mountain, and the Jews, the Israelites, would not be worshipping at Jerusalem either.

What is Christ saying here? What Luke 21 says: we would “fall by the edge of the sword”, and be “led away captive into all nations”, carried away as slaves into all nations. We fell by the sword in 70 AD, and being led into all nations is a process of time; it didn't all happen in 70 AD. Jerusalem would be “trodden down of the Gentiles”, occupied by heathens, until Christ returns and destroys the Gentiles.

In 70 AD most of us fled into Africa, formed communities, built cities and mingled amongst the Hamitic tribes. Esau drew maps pinpointing where the tribes were all over Africa, the Levite cities of Nigeria, Bnei Ephraim on the slave coast, the Jewish kingdoms, because slavery was not coincidence. Slavery was war.

precepts.text: Israel falls by the edge of Rome's sword, is led captive into all nations, and Jerusalem is trodden down of the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled: the strange slips.
precepts.point: Thou shalt plant pleasant plants and set it with strange slips: a slip is a cutting from a plant, so strange branches, Esau, not the people of the covenant, set in the land.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

precepts.why:
“In that day shall his strong cities be as a forsaken bough, and an uppermost branch, which they left because of the children of Israel: and there shall be desolation.” We were moved out of the land. Why? “Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength.” We have not been mindful of him. “Therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants, and shalt set it with strange slips.”

What is a slip? A cutting from a plant, a branch or twig. Strange slips are strange branches: Esau. They are strange, not the people of the book, not the people of the covenant, set into the land. Christ said the same thing about strange slips coming into the land.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the real Israelites fell by the edge of Rome's sword. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: captive means slaves, carried into all nations.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.” Christ is telling you the Gentiles are going to take over the land. That is what Isaiah said about the strange slips, the strange people who would take the land while the real children of Israel were scattered. And these leaders who bring out that they are not the real Jews disappear and die; we are the last ones standing.

precepts.text: Signs in the sun, moon and stars, eclipses and blood moons, distress of nations with perplexity, the sea roaring and men's hearts failing for fear: we are in verse 25 going into 26, and when these begin, look up, for your redemption draweth nigh, so clean yourselves up now.
precepts.point: All the tribes of the earth mourn and he sends his angels to gather his elect from the four winds: the elect is Jacob and Israel, not the Baptist church nor all races, and some Israelites who never heard still have to be fetched.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Luke tells the same coming, and shows where we are in it. “And there shall be signs in the sun”, like a solar eclipse, “and in the moon”, blood moons and lunar eclipses, “and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations”: we are seeing that now. “With perplexity”: perplexity means confusion. “The sea and the waves roaring”: the nations roaring.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” That is war. “And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” Right now we are in verse 25 going into the top part of verse 26.

“And when these things begin to come to pass”: the signs in the sun, the moon and the stars, the distress of nations with perplexity. “Then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” We are supposed to be looking up and lifting up our heads, knowing redemption is soon to come.

But we know the order of what is going to happen: tribulation, war, then Christ. So this is our time to clean ourselves up and get right with the Lord, because the time is drawing close.

precepts.text: Signs in the sun, moon, and stars, blood moons and eclipses; distress of nations with perplexity, confusion: they say Venezuela was drug dealers and Iraq had weapons of mass destruction, but Maduro, Gaddafi, and Iran sold oil outside the dollar; when white people say it is complex, it is simple and they do not want you to know. Men's hearts failing them for fear, but not us, because wisdom is our stability; the powers of heaven, America, England, France, Germany, shall be shaken; then the Son of man in a cloud. Look up, for your redemption draweth nigh. But one word in the verse, perplexity, is Jacob's trouble; the great tribulation comes before he returns, so do not say he might come tomorrow.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is all wisdom, Sirach 19:20, and in all wisdom is the performance of the law: be about it, not just talk about it. If you do not fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

note.label: Hope Amid Destruction

precepts.why:
Luke 21 shows people who are unstable in all their ways, wavering like the waves of the sea. “And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars”: eclipses of the sun, lunar eclipses, what they call blood moons. “and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity”: we are living in that time now. Perplexity means confusion. They said Venezuela was drug dealers, as they did with Manuel Noriega; they said Iraq had weapons of mass destruction and did not find one bomb. Anytime white people say it is a complex issue, it is something very easy that they don't want you to know: Maduro was selling his oil in foreign currencies, not the United States dollar; Iran was doing the same; Gaddafi wanted to.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth.” Why are they afraid? We are not afraid, because wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times: this is what the Bible was talking about, while everybody else is confused. “for the powers of heaven shall be shaken”: America, England, France, Germany.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” It is going to be almost time to go home.

But there is more to the one word perplexity: it goes into Jacob's trouble, the great tribulation that comes to try us. People want to skip the tribulation and say, war, Christ might come back tomorrow. No he won't. Jacob's trouble has to come to pass first.

precepts.text: Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things. Pray for prophecy to be fulfilled and that the enemy's plots be exposed, and that you are worthy to stand before Christ when it comes.
precepts.point: Take ye heed, watch and pray, for ye know not when the time is. Stay ready.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
“Take ye heed, watch and pray”, and Christ tells us what to watch and pray for: “Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.”

Watch and pray for the destruction of their wicked devices: that the traps, the plots and the lies of the enemy be exposed and broken. Ask the Most High to show you.

Pray for prophecy to be fulfilled. And pray that you are worthy to stand before Christ when these things come. We see all this unfolding, the nations moving and the empire declining, so the prayer is not for these things to be stopped but for us to be found worthy to escape them and stand before the Son of man.

precepts.point: I loved Jacob and hated Esau and laid his mountains waste. They shall call them the border of wickedness, the people against whom the Lord hath indignation forever.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
Esau's judgment was deferred for a time, and Christ gave the time: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

There is a set time that has to be fulfilled for these heathen nations, starting with Esau at the top: the same spirit of Cain in rulership. But it is temporary.

Through the process of time, waiting generation after generation for his judgment, Esau has forgotten it, or at least his pomp and pride make him think he is untouchable. Obadiah says, “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”, “that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” And who blames him? Look at what they just did to the air defenses Russia and China supplied. Trump now talks like that, of taking Venezuela and coming after Colombia and Mexico, and boasts that it was so fast and violent.

But it is prophesied who will bring him down. All those he dealt with will turn against him, and then Christ and his elect will have the glory and the honor to take him down. “evil shall hunt the violent man to overthrow him.” When the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled, his time is up.

precepts.text: Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.
precepts.point: The falling away was Israel's fall to Rome in 70 AD. Those in Jerusalem now are the Gentiles who tread it down.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“For that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” The day is the day of Christ, when he comes back in flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God. But first there has to be a falling away. What is that? Christ tells us.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword.” The Israelites fell by the sword of the Romans; we fell in 70 AD. “And shall be led away captive into all nations”: we fell away into captivity and were dispersed into all nations. That is the falling away. Deuteronomy 28 has to be fulfilled: the day of Christ will not come until Israel first goes into captivity for the evil they did.

“And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles.” So Netanyahu is a Gentile. That is what Christ said. The Jewish people there, the fake Jews, are Gentiles, thus saith the Lord. The ones starving out the Palestinians, bombing them and causing all kinds of ruckus in Iran are not the children of God.

Then “that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” Esau, the man of sin, has to be revealed to the whole planet, until everybody knows and agrees that this is the son of perdition, the devil on earth. America, with its long list of countries bombed and leaders overthrown, is the most powerful villain: Mystery Babylon the Great.

precepts.text: I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.
precepts.point: The Lord consumes him with the spirit of his mouth, speaking through his witnesses, and destroys him with the brightness of his coming.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work”: that is Rome, already working in the apostles’ time, “until he be taken out of the way.” “And then shall that Wicked be revealed.” Why does the wicked need to be revealed? Because he does not present himself as the wicked. He has transformed into an angel of light, into Lucifer, and people think he is the righteous. But God’s witnesses, the Israelites, the prophets that are waking up, will testify who the wicked is and reveal him: the so-called white man, the nation of Edom, the people God hates. For years we have said it and many did not believe; now he is showing you who he is.

Then: “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming.” Two things: consuming him with the spirit of his mouth, and destroying him with the brightness of his coming. What is the spirit of his mouth?

“For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all your adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.” That mouth and wisdom is Christ speaking through us, the Holy Spirit dwelling in us, so that nobody can gainsay us. That is the kind of power the Lord has given us.

So as we teach the word of God, the wicked are being consumed with the spirit of the Lord’s mouth, because we are bringing forth judgment. The Lord speaks through His witnesses, and their testimony condemns the wicked before his destruction at the brightness of Christ’s coming.

precepts.text: Ye shall be brought before kings and rulers for my name's sake.
precepts.point: The Pharisees took counsel with the Herodians how they might destroy him.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
The Pharisees took counsel with the Herodians against Christ, and Christ told his followers they would face the same. Mark says: “they shall deliver you up to councils; and in the synagogues ye shall be beaten: and ye shall be brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.” The rulers are our own people; the kings are the heathen, like Herod and the Caesars, like Nero. The testimony is against them both, the heathen and our own people, through the scriptures.

Luke says it too: “But before all these, they shall lay their hands on you, and persecute you, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name’s sake.” Kings like Agrippa; rulers like the Pharisees, the Sadducees and the scribes.

Why do the rulers of our own people do this? Isaiah says, “For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered.” They were evil and rebellious then and they are evil and rebellious now. They are the builders: “The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.” The rulers, whose eyes he covered in darkness because they were wicked, refused Christ.

So when the followers of Christ are mocked, defamed and delivered up by their own skinfolk to the kings of the earth, it is the same thing that was done to Christ. They are brought before kings and rulers for his name's sake, for a testimony against them.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:

Jerusalem compassed with armies is the siege Deuteronomy 28 speaks of, the enemy besieging thee in all thy gates. The siege of 70 AD fulfilled this curse: the same famine that made a woman boil her son in Samaria in the days of the kings came upon Jerusalem when the Romans compassed it.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” That city is under the Gentiles now: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

Israel fell by the edge of the sword and was led away captive into all nations, and Jerusalem, the joy of the whole earth, is trodden down of the Gentiles. Esau coveted it and took it by violence, and he holds it only until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

note.label: Psalm 48: Zion the Joy of the Whole Earth

precepts.why:
“Let mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah be glad, because of thy judgments.” Israel is to rejoice when the Most High brings fear upon the nations, and Christ describes that fear: “there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring; Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.”

The nations are perplexed and in distress right now over the coronavirus, hearts failing them for fear. Israel with understanding is to be rejoicing that redemption draws near. While the nations are afraid, Israel should gather together, get the pantry and the food and the house and the spirit in order, and rejoice rather than run around in fear. “thy right hand is full of righteousness”, and his judgments are Zion's gladness.

precepts.text: In your patience possess your souls; while we cry out how long, do not lose faith, Israel.
precepts.point: We ask the question, how long shall the wicked triumph.
